newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's wise men see 2.5 pct growth in 97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Germany's wise men see 2.5 pct growth in 97 - paper.

text.p: Germany's government panel of five independent economic advisors sees the national economy growing by 2.5 percent next year while unemployment remains high and inflation benign, the Bild newspaper said on Thursday.
Bild released extracts of a report to be presented on Friday by the panel -- the so-called "wise men" -- which saw unemployment averaging 4.1 million and inflation at 1.75 percent in 1997.

The growth forecast was in line with the view published recently by six leading research institutes, and joins a broad consensus that the recovery will gather pace after the economy expands by around one percent this year.

The panel also forecast that the total public sector budget deficit would total 114 billion marks. Bild did not say what the deficit would be when expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP).
Finance Minister Theo Waigel is aiming to cut the German budget deficit below ceiling of three percent of GDP set by the Maastricht treaty to qualify for European monetary union.

The institutes had predicted that the deficit would hit 3.5 percent, but Waigel has since agreed three billion marks in extra spending cuts with ministers in Germany's centre-right coalition government to try and hit his deficit goal.
